competitive_landscape: Guanabara Bay is served by mass-market ferries (CCR Barcas); Costa Verde by schooners and ferries; coastal towns by road. No foiling incumbent; both a mass-transit upgrade and a premium island-hopping play exist.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II covers Guanabara Bay commutes and the Costa Verde island mesh (Angra, Ilha Grande, Paraty bay).
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) opens the Rio↔Búzios (~95 nm) and Rio↔Paraty (~110 nm) coastal trunks.

precedents.why_it_matters: The Costa Verde reproduces a dense multi-island bay paradise, paired here with a mass bay-commute upgrade like other major-city harbours.

regulatory_note: Brazil flag; Marinha do Brasil / ANTAQ + Capitania dos Portos certification; state transport concessions for bay ferries; Ilha Grande is an environmental protection area.
seasonality: Year-round; peak Dec–Mar (Brazilian summer + Carnival); calmer seas autumn; afternoon sea breeze typical.

summary: Rio combines a large daily Guanabara Bay ferry-commute market (Rio↔Niterói carries huge volumes) with one of the world's great island-hopping coasts to the south: the Costa Verde, where Angra dos Reis fronts the 360-island Ilha Grande Bay and Paraty anchors a colonial-luxury scene. Búzios to the east is a chic resort peninsula. Short Costa Verde legs are Pioneer II; the longer Rio↔Búzios and Rio↔Paraty runs are Quanta-LR trunks. The combination of mass commute demand and premium island-hopping is rare.
tagline: A massive coastal metropolis plus the Costa Verde island paradise — Guanabara Bay commutes and the Angra/Ilha Grande archipelago.
